Claude Campus Ambassador Programme 2026.

September 3, 2026 4 minutes read
Applications are now open for the 2026 Claude Campus Ambassador Program. The programme supports student-led AI initiatives at universities and invites undergraduate students, graduate students, PhD students and postdocs to help create communities around AI learning, building and research.
Selected ambassadors receive a $3,600 stipend , Anthropic API credits, access to Anthropic guest speakers and membership in a global ambassador community. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis , meaning interested candidates are encouraged to apply early.

Program Duration

* This is a full school year program that runs from September 2026 to June 2027.
The Anthropic Campus Ambassador Program

* Students anywhere in the world can apply.

Student and campus tech ambassador programs

How student and campus tech ambassador programs work, who they are for, and how to find vetted listings.
By Davide Carlomagno · Updated 2026-07-25

Why campus programs exist

Companies invest in campus experts and student ambassadors to grow authentic developer communities at universities—clubs, workshops, and peer mentoring—not just coupon codes.

What students should expect

Expect public speaking or workshop practice, community organizing, and content creation. Strong programs offer mentorship, credits, swag, and career visibility—not only referral payouts.

Find listings here

Start with the Student & Campus category hub, then open program pages for requirements (often enrollment status or regional limits). Submit campus programs you know that meet our editorial rules.

* You participated and submitted a project in at least one Technovation Challenge season
* You must be between the ages of 13 and 18 as of October 1 of the year of application

Match fit, not just brand prestige

The visit provided an opportunity to discuss the relationship between Bangladesh and the Nagoya University and explore possibilities for future collaboration.
Nagoya University President Naoshi Sugiyama and Vice President Norimi Mizutani hosted the Ambassador at Toyoda Auditorium on the Higashiyama Campus. The two sides used the occasion to review the current state of academic exchanges and consider ways to develop them further.
Nagoya University currently has department-level agreements with three Bangladeshi institutions: Bangladesh Agricultural University (since 2000), the Department of Physics at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (since 2008), and the Faculty of Social Sciences at the University of Dhaka (since 2010).
